title: Newcastle University, Park View Student Village: fire safety strategy for six single-stair residential blocks
jurisdiction: England, UK (Newcastle upon Tyne, Richardson Road campus). COMPARATIVE NON-ALBERTA RECORD; no Alberta applicability asserted.
code_edition: Building Regulations 2010 (p.3). BS 9991 and BS 9999 cited without edition year. Approved Document B paragraph references (12.6, 12.7, Diagram 40) without a stated edition. Unknown if unstated.
document_date: 19 October 2018 (Rev D, final issue; first issue 12 September 2016)

facts.text: Six single-stair student residential blocks on the Richardson Road campus, 8.3 m to 25 m tall (to the topmost storey). BS 9991 is the basis of the strategy, supplemented by BS 9999 where applicable, for Building Regulations 2010 purposes.
Revision history: revision B (16 December 2016) 'revised to reflect meeting with Building Control'; revision D (19 October 2018) is the final issue.
Blocks 2, 3 and 4 have a fire-fighting shaft with a fire-fighting lift and dry rising main. Load-bearing elements are 90 minutes for buildings above 18 m and 60 minutes below 18 m.

Cluster accommodation: the maximum travel distance in the common corridor is about 11 m. The text says this 'does not follow the guidance contained within BS 9991' and gives reasons, comparing it with a traditional flat with a protected entrance.
Plant-room service corridor: travel distance exceeds the recommendation, 'nevertheless it has been agreed with Newcastle Building Control'.

Rooftop plantroom (s.3.5.8): 'Building Control have raised concerns that a fire in a rooftop plantroom could result in fire spreading into the stair core'. The consultant's opinion is that the risk is low because of a protected lobby and fire-resisting wall, and a stair vent opens on smoke detection.

External wall (s.5.1): rooftop plant cladding uses coated steel composite panels with a PUR/PIR core. For the three blocks above 18 m, 'the material forming the core ... [is] not expected to satisfy' the Approved Document B para 12.7 limited-combustibility recommendation. Mitigations are listed (plant above the core only; panels on a concrete slab, not connected to the façade; lower-floor walls to ADB).

Façade surface classes by height: Blocks 1, 5 and 6 (18 m or less) to Class 0 or B-s3,d2 for parts up to 18 m. Blocks 2-4 (above 18 m): Index I not more than 20 (BS 476-6) or Class C-s3,d2 (BS EN 13501) for the lower wall, and not less than Class 0 or B-s3,d2 above 18 m.
Space separation (s.5.2): 'it is not expected that external walls will require any fire resistance'; calculations 'can be provided if required by the authorities'.
